title: Runbook + oncall integration for auto-rollback (alert links + paging policy)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Context
Auto-rollback will trigger based on latency/error SLO breaches. To keep MTTR low and prevent confusion during incidents, automated rollback events must be wired into the oncall workflow with (1) correct routing (page vs ticket) and (2) actionable links (runbook, rollout, dashboards, audit event).

Scope
1) Runbook links in alerts / notifications
- Ensure every auto-rollback alert/notification includes:
  - Primary runbook link: Confluence runbook “Auto-rollback on SLO breach”
  - Rollout details link (Console rollout page) with tenant/route/model/version pre-selected
  - Dashboard link for the relevant monitor (latency or error SLO) scoped to route/model/region/tier
  - Audit log query link (where applicable) for the rollback execution event

2) Oncall routing
- Ensure notifications go to the correct destinations:
  - Slack: #eng-oncall (high signal) and #eng-platform (FYI / engineering follow-up)
  - PagerDuty: Redwood Platform (primary) with SRE escalation for multi-tenant / broad-impact scenarios
  - Ticketing: create Jira ticket for non-urgent / expected rollouts noise

3) Define “page vs ticket” policy for auto-rollback events
- Document and implement routing rules to reduce paging fatigue while ensuring true incidents page.

Out of scope
- Changing the rollback decision algorithm (handled in ENG-2314 / ENG-2315)
- Building new alerting infrastructure (use existing alert templates + incident-bot)

Acceptance criteria
A) Links are present and correct
- Alert payload contains runbook_url, rollout_url, dashboard_url, and audit_event_id (when rollback executed).
- Links are tenant-safe (do not leak another tenant’s data) and resolve without requiring manual URL edits.
- Rollout URL points to current rollout attempt and includes verdict state (BREACH/HEALTHY/UNKNOWN) and reason.

B) Routing rules implemented and documented
- For P0/P1 impact cases (see matrix below) we page the oncall.
- For lower-impact or ambiguous cases we create a ticket and post to Slack without paging.
- Routing policy is captured in the runbook and referenced from alert templates.

C) Dry run validation
- Game day / synthetic SLO breach test confirms:
  - Slack message includes links and is readable
  - PagerDuty incident contains the same context
  - Ticket creation works and includes enough details to debug later

Paging vs Ticketing matrix (v1)
Page (PagerDuty) when ANY of:
1) Auto-rollback executed for Dedicated or Private tenant (tier in {dedicated, private})
2) >= 3 rollbacks triggered within 30 minutes across distinct tenants OR distinct regions (possible shared infra issue)
3) Rollback fails to execute (executor error / stuck) after breach decision
4) Error SLO breach is 5xx-driven (server errors) AND affects hosted shared tier at scale (detected by “multi-tenant” condition)

Ticket (Jira) + Slack-only when ANY of:
1) Auto-rollback executed for hosted self-serve tier with low traffic (min-traffic guardrail barely met) and rollback succeeds
2) Verdict is UNKNOWN due to monitor staleness/outage < 15 minutes (post to #eng-platform + create ticket)
3) Canary warm-up suppression triggered (expected during first N minutes) — informational only

Notes
- “Multi-tenant” is determined by evaluator metric rollbacks_count{window=30m} and/or incident-bot aggregation logic; exact thresholds can be tuned post-GA.
- If monitor outage persists >= 15 minutes and affects multiple services/regions, treat as an observability incident and page.

Implementation plan
1) Update incident-bot notification template for auto-rollback events
- Include runbook URL and rollout URL
- Ensure message includes: tenant, route, model, from_version, to_version, region, tier, trigger_slo (latency/error), window, observed_value, threshold, baseline_value (if applicable), decision_trace_id

2) Update alert templates (observability-pack)
- Add runbook link and standard “next actions” section that maps to the runbook sections

3) Document routing and triage steps in runbook
- Add a dedicated “Alert routing: page vs ticket” section
- Add “What to check first” section with dashboard links and expected patterns for false positives

References / links
- Confluence runbook (draft): sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-auto-rollback-on-slo-breach.json
- Dashboard/alert spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/rollout-slo-dashboards-and-alerting.json
- Audit logging spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/rollout-and-rollback-audit-events.json
- incident-bot PR: sources/github/incident-bot/pr-133.json
- Observability dashboards PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-944.json
comments: 2025-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): Please avoid paging on single-tenant hosted rollbacks unless rollback fails. We’ve had paging fatigue from noisy “self-healing” events in other systems. +1 to paging on Dedicated/Private by default.

2025-02-04 (Marissa Cole): Console team can guarantee a stable rollout URL format: /console/rollouts/{rollout_id}?tenant={tenant_id}. Please include it in all notifications; it’s the fastest way for support/CS to confirm what happened.

2025-02-06 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented incident-bot message template changes behind feature flag `incident_bot.autorollback_v1`. Added fields: runbook_url, rollout_url, dashboard_url. Pending review from SRE for paging thresholds.

2025-02-08 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed monitor-outage handling: UNKNOWN verdict should never page unless duration >= 15m and multiple tenants. Please ensure alert copy is explicit: “No rollback executed; monitoring data unavailable.”

2025-02-11 (Miles Thornton): Game day note: when we simulated latency regression, the Slack message was good but the dashboard link was missing region scoping. Please ensure the dashboard URL includes region and tier filters (otherwise confusing).

2025-02-13 (Hannah Rivera): Fixed dashboard URL scoping; now uses monitor identity labels (route/model/region/tier) to generate deep links. Also added executor failure condition to page (rollback failed) as P1.

2025-02-19 (Rafael Mendes): Verified in staging via synthetic SLO breach harness: (1) Slack message posted to #eng-oncall with runbook + console link, (2) PD incident created only for Dedicated scenario, (3) hosted self-serve scenario created Jira ticket and Slack-only. Marking done; tuning to be tracked separately post-GA.
